observations: F2-WP-100 resolve_unifieddb_path forbids relative explicit DB paths and resolves explicit pointer/environment authorities independently of process CWD.
F2-WP-100 fails closed when multiple explicit authorities select different canonical paths.

F2-WP-103 CanonicalDeliveryStore demonstrates the accepted writer pattern: an already-existing SQLite connection must bind to the exact resolution plus fingerprinted device/inode/real path, and the store never invents a second database path.

WP206 claims a real subprocess/process restart. A restart therefore crosses a fresh resolver/open boundary; persistence evidence is insufficient if process 2 merely reuses a path string supplied by process 1 without independently re-resolving current canonical authority.

The existing WP206 review delta 01 covers WAL/logical checkpoint identity. This review is intentionally nonduplicate: it covers cross-process authority re-resolution and path-drift/CWD/explicit-authority falsification.
falsifiers: Start process A with one absolute explicit FRANKENSTEIN2_DB path, persist the typed Agency checkpoint, exit, then start process B from a different working directory with the same explicit authority. Process B must independently resolve the identical real path and recover the checkpoint; CWD must not influence durable truth.

Start process B with FRANKENSTEIN2_DB and pointer authority simultaneously selecting different files. Restart/replay must fail closed with UnifiedDBAuthorityConflict before any Agency checkpoint is read, written, replayed, or advanced.

Replace or redirect the selected SQLite file between process A and process B while preserving the old path spelling. Re-resolution plus fingerprint binding must reject file-identity drift before checkpoint replay.
Search the test sandbox after the restart path completes: no second .db file outside the independently resolved canonical path may contain WP206-owned Agency tables/rows.

Run the same restart test with process B launched under an unrelated CWD and without any relative-path fallback. A passing test that depends on repository CWD is a failure of the canonical persistence claim.
completion_deficit: WP206 repository-hosted restart acceptance should not be granted until the subprocess test proves fresh process-B UnifiedDB authority resolution/fingerprint binding and fail-closed authority/path drift in addition to the separate WAL/checkpoint-identity discriminators.
next_exact_action: Active F2-WP-206 mutation authority should incorporate the cross-process resolution/path-drift falsifiers into its deterministic subprocess CI without creating another DB/state authority.
